corrections.critique: Strongest feature: Ehrman directly dismantles the inference from enduring unanimity to authentic authorship by presenting historically instructive counterexamples whose conventional attributions remained remarkably stable despite widespread scholarly rejection of authenticity. Principal limitation: The analogies do not fully reproduce the claimed chronological proximity, geographical distribution, or independent testimonial diversity of Gospel attribution, so they undermine sufficiency more decisively than comparative evidential weight. Live burden: The reply must still explain why earlier distributed agreement deserves authentication-level confidence rather than reflecting durable naming convention, while proponents must distinguish their transmission mechanism from the demonstrably persistent misattribution represented by Barnabas and Second Clement. Locked score: The very strong score of 89 appropriately recognizes an exceptionally relevant, logically disciplined full answer while preserving meaningful deductions for underdeveloped chronological and evidentiary disanalogies.

Strongest feature: Licona clearly separates formal textual anonymity from absent community knowledge, carefully qualifies Papias concerning canonical Matthew, and uses Justin to support the plausibility of traditional connections before Irenaeus. Principal limitation: Genre convention merely neutralizes one inference from anonymity and neither authenticates the later names nor answers examples of persistent conventional misattribution or the proposed authority-driven naming mechanism. Live burden: The reply needs a historically specific transmission account connecting early testimony to the canonical Gospels, while explaining why stable titles reflect preserved authorship knowledge rather than retrospective attribution and directly confronting the unanswered counterexamples. Locked score: The strong score of 79 properly rewards coherent, cautious, and relevant chronological evidence while reflecting partial responsiveness, limited authentication force, and failure to contact two decisive components of the opposing challenge.
